title: Construction contract risk identification based on knowledge-augmented language models
task: 施工合同风险识别与知识增强审查
inputData: 施工合同条款 + 合同事实知识 + 专家条款-审查对知识库
contribution: 提出免微调的施工合同风险识别框架，将自然语言形式的事实知识和专家审查知识向量化并按合同检查点检索，为GPT-4提供项目条款与历史条款-审查对上下文，模拟专家合同审查过程。
abstract: The paper develops a tuning-free knowledge-augmented LLM method for construction contract risk identification. A natural-language domain knowledge base stores factual contract knowledge and expert clause-review knowledge; relevant project clauses and clause-review pairs are retrieved and injected into prompts for risk identification. The approach is evaluated on real construction contracts and compared with standard prompting.
methodology: The methodology has four implemented parts: constructing a domain-specific knowledge base, retrieving relevant project clauses, retrieving expert clause-review pairs, and prompting the LLM. Contract sections are segmented and vectorized. The implementation stores the knowledge in Milvus with HNSW indexing and hybrid search; the reported knowledge base includes 48 specific conditions and 8 clause-review pairs, retrieving the top five relevant project clauses and top three clause-review examples. GPT-4 generates repeated risk-review responses and consistency/voting strategies are used to improve robustness.
results: Case studies on practical construction contracts show that augmenting GPT-4 with factual and expert contract knowledge produces risk reviews that are more aligned with expert reasoning than standard prompting. The paper emphasizes qualitative/case-based validation rather than a single large aggregate benchmark and discusses how the LLM combines retrieved factual context with expert-review examples.
taskEn: Construction contract risk identification and knowledge-augmented review
inputDataEn: Construction contract clauses plus factual contract knowledge and an expert clause-review knowledge base
operationEvidence: The system retrieves relevant clauses and expert review cases from the domain knowledge base and uses them to identify contradictions, omissions, and contractual risks.
